lines.text: How does Face ID work in the dark?
It sprays thousands of dots onto your face.
How they bend becomes a depth map.
A locked chip turns that map into math.
A flat photo has no depth, so it fails.
Pitch dark is fine. Five misses, and it wants your passcode.

post.title: How does Face ID work in the dark?
post.caption:
How does Face ID work in the dark? 🌑

It doesn't need your room's light. The TrueDepth camera at the top of your iPhone projects thousands of invisible infrared dots onto your face and reads how they land to build a depth map, plus an infrared image of your face. A part of the chip that's walled off in the Secure Enclave turns that into math and compares it with the face you enrolled; it never leaves the phone. Because it reads depth, not just a picture, it's built to resist photos and masks, and Apple puts the chance of a random person unlocking your iPhone at less than 1 in 1,000,000. After five failed tries it asks for your passcode.
Save this for the next time someone asks how it sees in the dark.

Apple Platform Security, Face ID and Touch ID security: the TrueDepth camera projects and reads thousands of infrared dots to form a depth map with a 2D infrared image, signed and sent to the Secure Enclave; randomized sequences counter digital and physical spoofs
